answer: Each agent earns influence only after completing small jobs with counterparties who already have established histories; a new identity starts with no weight. When counterparties later reveal a shared controller or repeatedly endorse one another, the system discounts that cluster’s endorsements and propagates the reduction through the trust graph like a ripple. A sparrow-sized fake account therefore cannot amplify a claim alone: the attacker must build many independent histories over time, paying for real work and risking detection across a longer horizon.
